text:
suyog: Quick RFC follow-up 1: proposal to tighten the decision-graph contract so the runtime can request 'strict' vs 'best_effort' scoring and attach a short telemetry token for sim/ops correlation.
jessica: can you sketch the minimal API shape? example payload please.
suyog: sketch: decision_id, objective (latency|cost|region), mode (strict|best_effort), telemetry_token (optional), decision_hints (optional small map).
ben: ops really wants a stable id to join traces. recommend reserving a UUID namespace for decision_id.
rahul: big question: how do strict vs best_effort change fallback semantics? sounds like it impacts preemption and hedging.
suyog: correct. strict => disallow additional fallback routes unless the route explicitly marks itself degradable. best_effort => runtime may pick fallbacks based on latency/capacity signals.
sam: security question: will telemetry_token leak tenant metadata? any PII concerns?
jessica: token must be opaque, TTL-limited, signed by KMS. runtime validates signature; token contains no PII. private deployments use customer-signed tokens. hosted uses redwood-signed index tokens.
ops-bot: deploy-plan reminder: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% (manual approval at 50%).
ben: sim needs stable mapping between decision_id and sim_case. also we should keep decision_id reasonably short for storage indexing.
rahul: add decision_hints fields: cost_budget_micros and latency_sla_ms (soft constraints) so policy can surface tradeoffs to the runtime. keep hints optional and optional to ignore.
suyog: agreed. canonical contract = decision_id, objective, mode, optional telemetry_token, optional decision_hints.
jessica: wire format: protobuf v2, runtime should ignore unknown fields. require header x-policy-version to gate compatibility.
sam: perf note: telemetry_token increases request size. make it optional and compress to ~32 bytes base62 token.
ben: base62 token + signed index ok. compressing the token avoids per-request inflation.
rahul: how does this affect metrics? we need to avoid cardinality explosion in Console.
ops-bot: @ops-team: add runbook entry to detect anomalous decision_id spikes / cardinality increases.
ben: sim/ops join key proposal: decision_id + route_hash + timestamp_bucket. will share PR with examples.
jessica: compat plan: runtime accepts legacy payloads; default mode=best_effort if absent. proto addition is backward-compatible if we ignore unknowns.
ben: rollout plan: schema PR -> runtime guard flag -> sim harness update -> gradual canary. estimate 2 weeks if no blockers.
sam: console: add telemetry-metrics tag so Console can filter traces and flows by decision_id. ensure tag is optional and capped.
jessica: security nit: document TTL for tokens and revocation semantics; include KMS key rotation impact.
suyog: ops items: need pipeline to join traces -> decision events -> sim runs. ben/ops to propose join keys by EOD.
ben: opening schema PR now, will include an example proto and short migration guide.
rahul: I'll update the fallback semantics doc to include strict vs best_effort semantics and show examples: canary flow, preemption cases, and cost tradeoffs.
sam: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: scheduled canary window at 2026-03-25T15:00Z.
suyog: action items recap: ben -> schema PR + sim join keys; jessica -> runtime guard + x-policy-version validation; ops -> runbook + trace-join pipeline; rahul -> fallback doc update; check-in Fri.
jessica: agree to add example invalidation flow: token revocation -> how runtime rejects and falls back.
suyog: good call. I'll add a short appendix to the RFC with revocation and TTL guidance.
ben: thanks, starting PRs now.
